body:
Thanks for a reproducer,

I've had a quick look and I don't think `X-Forwarded-Prefix` has even been even considered, so it should be an enhancement request, not supporting one of the non-standard `X-Forwarded`  headers is not a bug.
@froque Sorry, I got confused, looks like it is handled in the code

Looks like it is a REST issue, as there is a `ForwardedPrefixHeaderTest` in Vert.x HTTP.
@froque Can you please give us a favor and confirm it independently, that it works with the Vert.x route ?

> Looks like it is a REST issue, as there is a `ForwardedPrefixHeaderTest` in Vert.x HTTP. [@froque](https://github.com/froque) Can you please give us a favor and confirm it independently, that it works with the Vert.x route ?

not really sure how to do that.

This looks like a legitimate issue with Quarkus REST. 
@FroMage does Renarde perhaps handle this?

Definitely looks like a legitimate feature, absolutely.

Renarde does not handle this, and I never noticed it because while I am using reverse proxies a lot, I never change the path: "only" the scheme, host and port.

I have to say I'm surprised that `path` does not appear to be supported by the now-standard `Forwarded` header: https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7239 for a reason I can't imagine.
Actually, I can't find any authoritative source defining `X-Forwarded-Path` online :-/
